mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace an AMG GLA 35 engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: An AMG GLA 35 engine replacement typically costs between £3,500 and £7,800 depending on condition type and whether fitting is included. M260 2.0-litre turbo units range from £3,500 to £7,800 supply only. Rebuilt M260 (AMG GLA 35): £3,500-£7,800 supply only. Reconditioned units: £3,800-£5,800. Used engines from breakers: £2,200-£4,000 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £1,000-£1,800 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: Is the M260 engine in the AMG GLA 35 reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M260 is a high-performance engine that delivers impressive power, but it has several well-documented issues that owners should be aware of. Post-facelift (2023+) M260 engines with 48V MHEV appear more reliable. Cylinder head / valve seat defect - extended warranty covers many 2019-2022 models. Timing chain tensioner wear causing cold-start rattle. CAMTRONIC system failures (expensive to repair). Turbocharger wear and oil consumption. Regular oil changes every 5,000-7,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M260 cylinder head failure in an AMG GLA 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M260 cylinder head defect typically manifests as valve seat wear - symptoms can appear with minimal warning. Engine misfires or rough running. Loss of power and poor acceleration. Check engine light illuminated. Rough idle, particularly when warm. Some owners have reported failure as early as 11,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my AMG GLA 35 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., timing chain tensioner, turbocharger). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic cylinder head failure. Timing chain tensioner replacement: £450-£750 - do this at first sign of rattle. Cylinder head replacement: £2,500-£3,800 - for valve seat wear without piston damage. Full M260 rebuild: £4,500-£7,800 - for catastrophic failure or 80k+ miles. Given AMG GLA 35 values (£30,000-£50,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my AMG GLA 35 has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. AMG GLA 35 (2020-present): M260.920 (2.0L turbo, 306hp). Service history documents list engine type.

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on an AMG GLA 35. The transverse-mounted engine layout, 8-speed DCT gearbox alignment, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. Transverse engine mounting requires specialist alignment. 8G-DCT transmission alignment needs precise setup. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation required. AMG-specific calibration and adaptations needed. Specialist supply & fit costs £1,000-£1,800 - essential for an AMG.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz AMG GLA 35 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes-AMG GLA 35's M260 engine delivers impressive performance but has developed a well-documented reputation for specific, potentially serious failures. The cylinder head defect - affecting exhaust valve seats - is the most significant concern, with some owners requiring replacement at as little as 11,000 miles. Timing chain tensioner wear, CAMTRONIC system failures, and oil consumption also feature prominently. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common AMG GLA 35 engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.group: M260 Cylinder Head & Valve Seat Failure
problems.h4: M260 Cylinder Head & Valve Seat Failure - Why the AMG GLA 35 Misfires and Loses Power
problems.rootCause: A known defect with the exhaust valve seats in the M260 engine causes valve seat wear, leading to loss of compression, misfires, and eventually engine failure. Mercedes has acknowledged this issue with an extended warranty (15 years / 150,000 miles) covering many 2019-2022 models. The issue is particularly prevalent on AMG 35 series cars.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Cylinder Head Inspection & Valve Job
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove cylinder head, inspect valve seats, replace affected valves, pressure test
repairOptions.longevity: 20k-50k miles. Viable if caught early with minimal valve seat damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace entire cylinder head with updated casting, new valves, springs, seals
repairOptions.longevity: 30k-60k miles. Required if valve seat damage is extensive

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M260 with updated cylinder head, upgraded valve train components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary when valve failure has caused piston or bore damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical AMG GLA 35 is worth £30,000-£50,000 depending on age and mileage - the full replacement cost of £4,500-£7,800 is modest relative to vehicle value. Given the known cylinder head defect, many cars may qualify for Mercedes extended warranty coverage (15 years / 150,000 miles) - always check with your dealer before authorising any repair.
problems.recommendation: The M260 cylinder head issue is serious and can appear with minimal warning. If your AMG GLA 35 experiences misfires, rough running, or loss of power, have the cylinder head inspected immediately. Given that Mercedes has issued an extended warranty for this specific issue, contact your dealer first to determine if your vehicle is covered. If out of warranty, specialist cylinder head replacement at £2,500-£3,800 is significantly better value than dealer pricing.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M260 Mercedes Benz AMG GLA 35 engine prices

problems.group: M260 Timing Chain & CAMTRONIC System Issues
problems.h4: M260 Timing Chain & CAMTRONIC System Issues - Why the AMG GLA 35 Rattles on Start-Up
problems.rootCause: The M260 uses a timing chain drive with hydraulic tensioner. Over time, the tensioner can fail, allowing chain slack and producing a rattling noise on cold start. The CAMTRONIC variable valve lift system (A6560500001) can also fail - its repair is known to be very expensive. Post-facelift (2023+) M260 engines appear to be less prone to these issues.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioner with updated part (A2600502000), oil and filter change
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-60k miles. Viable if caught early with no chain stretch

repairOptions.tier: Major - Full Timing Chain Set & CAMTRONIC
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets, and CAMTRONIC actuator
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-80k miles. Required if rattling persists or fault codes present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M260 with new timing components, CAMTRONIC system
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if chain has jumped or CAMTRONIC failure caused valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On an AMG GLA 35 worth £30,000-£50,000, timing chain replacement at £1,500-£2,500 is a justifiable investment. Full engine replacement is only necessary for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: At the first sign of rattling on cold start, have the timing chain tensioner inspected immediately - ignoring it can lead to catastrophic engine failure. Mercedes Service Bulletin notes that timing chain noise alone may not cause engine damage if addressed promptly. For CAMTRONIC issues, specialist diagnosis is essential; the system is complex and repair costs can escalate quickly.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M260 Mercedes Benz AMG GLA 35 engine prices

problems.h4: M260 Turbocharger & Oil Consumption - High-Performance AMG Engine Wear
problems.rootCause: The M260's twin-scroll turbocharger operates at high boost pressures, generating significant heat. Insufficient cool-down periods after hard driving can coke the oil feed lines, restricting oil flow to the turbo bearings. Oil consumption is also a reported concern on higher-mileage M260 units.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace turbocharger, clean oil feed lines, replace oil and filter
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-70k miles. Viable if caught early with no internal engine debris

repairOptions.tier: Major - Turbo Plus Intercooler & Oil System Flush
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Turbo replacement plus intercooler removal, oil system flush, new oil cooler
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-70k miles. Required if turbo bearings have failed and shed debris

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M260 with new turbocharger, upgraded oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary when turbo debris has scored cylinder walls

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On an AMG GLA 35 worth £30,000-£50,000, turbocharger replacement at £1,500-£2,200 is a sensible repair. Full engine replacement is only justified for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: On an AMG GLA 35, do not cut corners on turbo maintenance. If you hear whistling or notice oil consumption above 1 litre per 1,000 miles, have the turbo inspected immediately. A specialist turbo replacement is painful but far less painful than a full engine rebuild. Also, fit a turbo timer or religiously idle the engine for 60 seconds after hard driving - it doubles turbo bearing life on high-performance turbocharged engines.
